title: Compactivation: A mechanochemical approach to carbons with superior porosity and exceptional performance for hydrogen and CO2 storage
material_description: PPY2 | polypyrrole-derived conventionally KOH-activated carbon, KOH/PPy = 2, 800 degC
purification_method: washed several times with 10 wt% HCl, then with distilled water to neutral pH (no stirring); dried at 120 degC for 3 h
activation_method: KOH chemical activation of polypyrrole: KOH/PPy mass ratio 2, KOH and PPy mixed in an agate mortar (no compaction step), heated in a horizontal furnace (alumina boat) at 3 degC/min to 800 degC under N2 flow and held 1 h
source_location: main p.6 (journal p.178), Figure 3a, series "PPY2 Excess" (open black circles), digitized
notes: low-pressure or partially hidden marker in a crowded region; position less certain; archive: F3a_PPY2_excess.json; BET range: 0.04-0.2; total pore volume from the amount of N2 adsorbed at P/Po = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other); NLDFT pore size distribution maxima 12/25 A (Table 1); N content ca. 0.75 wt% (text p.4; N carried over from the polypyrrole precursor, not described as doping; not coded as dopant); carbon yield 22 wt% (Table S1); precursor polypyrrole made with FeCl3 oxidant (pyrrole 3 g, 0.5 M FeCl3 200 mL, 2 h); isotherm point count: count 32 = 31 markers extracted + 1 marker near 0.7 bar not separable; measured on a Hiden IGA-003 gravimetric analyser; degassing: dried at 80 degC for 24 h, then degassed at 200 degC and 10^-10 bar for 4-6 h (duration range not stored); stated once for all H2 measurements (Experimental, main p.3); buoyancy correction and sample mass not stated; wt% convention not defined (the SI total formula adds 100 dV/(1+dV) to the excess wt%)
basis_evidence: SI p.2: "Our measurements provided the excess hydrogen uptake, which is the amount of hydrogen adsorbed in the carbons above that which would have been stored in the pores under similar conditions (temperature and pressure) assuming that there is zero energy of interaction between the hydrogen and the carbon pore walls." Excess and total are reported side by side (Tables 1, 3, S3, S4, S5; Figures 3, 5, 6).

purification_method: washed several times with 10 wt% HCl, then with distilled water to neutral pH (no stirring); dried at 120 degC for 3 h
activation_method: KOH chemical activation of polypyrrole: KOH/PPy mass ratio 2, KOH and PPy mixed in an agate mortar (no compaction step), heated in a horizontal furnace (alumina boat) at 3 degC/min to 800 degC under N2 flow and held 1 h
source_location: main p.6 (journal p.178), Figure 3a, series "PPY2 Excess" (open black circles), digitized
notes: archive: F3a_PPY2_excess.json; BET range: 0.04-0.2; total pore volume from the amount of N2 adsorbed at P/Po = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other); NLDFT pore size distribution maxima 12/25 A (Table 1); N content ca. 0.75 wt% (text p.4; N carried over from the polypyrrole precursor, not described as doping; not coded as dopant); carbon yield 22 wt% (Table S1); precursor polypyrrole made with FeCl3 oxidant (pyrrole 3 g, 0.5 M FeCl3 200 mL, 2 h); isotherm point count: count 32 = 31 markers extracted + 1 marker near 0.7 bar not separable; measured on a Hiden IGA-003 gravimetric analyser; degassing: dried at 80 degC for 24 h, then degassed at 200 degC and 10^-10 bar for 4-6 h (duration range not stored); stated once for all H2 measurements (Experimental, main p.3); buoyancy correction and sample mass not stated; wt% convention not defined (the SI total formula adds 100 dV/(1+dV) to the excess wt%)
basis_evidence: SI p.2: "Our measurements provided the excess hydrogen uptake, which is the amount of hydrogen adsorbed in the carbons above that which would have been stored in the pores under similar conditions (temperature and pressure) assuming that there is zero energy of interaction between the hydrogen and the carbon pore walls." Excess and total are reported side by side (Tables 1, 3, S3, S4, S5; Figures 3, 5, 6).

purification_method: washed several times with 10 wt% HCl, then with distilled water to neutral pH (no stirring); dried at 120 degC for 3 h
activation_method: KOH chemical activation of polypyrrole: KOH/PPy mass ratio 2, KOH and PPy mixed in an agate mortar; the KOH/PPy mixture was compacted for 10 min at a load of 10 t in a 1.3 cm die (740 MPa) before the thermal treatment ("compactivation"), heated in a horizontal furnace (alumina boat) at 3 degC/min to 800 degC under N2 flow and held 1 h
source_location: main p.6 (journal p.178), Figure 3a, series "MPPY2 Total" (filled red circles), digitized
notes: archive: F3a_MPPY2_total.json; BET range: 0.04-0.2; total pore volume from the amount of N2 adsorbed at P/Po = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other); NLDFT pore size distribution maxima 12/22 A (Table 1); N content ca. 0.75 wt% (text p.4; N carried over from the polypyrrole precursor, not described as doping; not coded as dopant); carbon yield 23 wt% (Table S1); precursor polypyrrole made with FeCl3 oxidant (pyrrole 3 g, 0.5 M FeCl3 200 mL, 2 h); total uptake calculated by the authors from the measured excess using the N2 total pore volume (SI p.2 equation); isotherm point count: total markers at low pressure are hidden behind the excess markers of the same run; count taken equal to the excess isotherm (the total is calculated point by point from the excess, SI p.2); measured on a Hiden IGA-003 gravimetric analyser; degassing: dried at 80 degC for 24 h, then degassed at 200 degC and 10^-10 bar for 4-6 h (duration range not stored); stated once for all H2 measurements (Experimental, main p.3); buoyancy correction and sample mass not stated; wt% convention not defined (the SI total formula adds 100 dV/(1+dV) to the excess wt%)
basis_evidence: SI p.2: "The total uptake is calculated from the excess storage by taking into account the amount of hydrogen compressed into the carbon pore volume space." with theta_T = theta_Exc + 100 x dH2 x VT/(1 + dH2 x VT), VT = pore volume from nitrogen or CO2 sorption; excess and total reported side by side.

purification_method: washed several times with 10 wt% HCl, then with distilled water to neutral pH (no stirring); dried at 120 degC for 3 h
activation_method: KOH chemical activation of polypyrrole: KOH/PPy mass ratio 3, KOH and PPy mixed in an agate mortar (no compaction step), heated in a horizontal furnace (alumina boat) at 3 degC/min to 800 degC under N2 flow and held 1 h
source_location: main p.6 (journal p.178), Figure 3b, series "PPY3 Excess" (open black circles), digitized
notes: archive: F3b_PPY3_excess.json; BET range: 0.04-0.2; total pore volume from the amount of N2 adsorbed at P/Po = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other); NLDFT pore size distribution maxima 12/26 A (Table 1); N content ca. 0.55 wt% (text p.4; N carried over from the polypyrrole precursor, not described as doping; not coded as dopant); carbon yield 19 wt% (Table S1); precursor polypyrrole made with FeCl3 oxidant (pyrrole 3 g, 0.5 M FeCl3 200 mL, 2 h); measured on a Hiden IGA-003 gravimetric analyser; degassing: dried at 80 degC for 24 h, then degassed at 200 degC and 10^-10 bar for 4-6 h (duration range not stored); stated once for all H2 measurements (Experimental, main p.3); buoyancy correction and sample mass not stated; wt% convention not defined (the SI total formula adds 100 dV/(1+dV) to the excess wt%)
basis_evidence: SI p.2: "Our measurements provided the excess hydrogen uptake, which is the amount of hydrogen adsorbed in the carbons above that which would have been stored in the pores under similar conditions (temperature and pressure) assuming that there is zero energy of interaction between the hydrogen and the carbon pore walls." Excess and total are reported side by side (Tables 1, 3, S3, S4, S5; Figures 3, 5, 6).
